1	"""A claimed spec, as a thing with parts rather than a bag of keys.
     2	
     3	A spec arrives as JSON and is held to the contract's schema before anything
     4	is done with it. Past that gate it becomes this: a small frozen record whose
     5	fields say what they hold, so the code that conducts a simulation asks for
     6	``spec.limits.max_turns`` instead of walking three dictionaries deep and
     7	trusting that each step is there.
     8	
     9	The gate and the type are deliberately the same step. Nothing builds one of
    10	these without validating first, which is what lets every reader below take
    11	the fields at face value.
    12	"""
    13	
    14	from __future__ import annotations
    15	
    16	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    17	from typing import Any
    18	
    19	from .contract import ContractViolation, validate_spec
    20	
    21	
    22	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    23	class MockTool:
    24	    """One tool name, and what egma answers when the agent calls it.
    25	
    26	    Already resolved when it arrives: the control plane worked the
    27	    project's defaults and the test's overrides into one answer per name
    28	    at run creation, so every simulation in one run sees one world and
    29	    there is nothing left here to merge.
    30	    """
    31	
    32	    tool_name: str
    33	    """The agent's own name for the tool, verbatim — the whole of how a
    34	    call is matched, and never parsed or folded."""
    35	
    36	    answer: dict[str, Any]
    37	    """What is served, in the shape it was authored in: ``{"answer": …}``
    38	    with the value the tool returns, or ``{"error": …}`` with the failure
    39	    it raises. Held whole rather than unpacked, so the bytes that go on
    40	    the wire are the bytes that were authored."""
    41	
    42	    delay_milliseconds: int
    43	    """How long egma holds the answer back, so a mocked backend takes as
    44	    long as the real one would."""
    45	
    46	    @property
    47	    def fails(self) -> bool:
    48	        """Whether this answer is the failure branch."""
    49	        return "error" in self.answer
    50	
    51	
    52	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    53	class PlatformCarrier:
    54	    """The SIP trunk a deployment uses for phone simulations.
    55	
    56	    The media backend is deployment configuration. It cannot ride this
    57	    block and cannot be selected by a work order.
    58	    """
    59	
    60	    trunk_address: str | None = None
    61	    trunk_number: str | None = None
    62	    trunk_username: str | None = None
    63	    trunk_password: str | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
    64	
    65	
    66	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    67	class PlatformSettings:
    68	    """The carrier part of deployment configuration on this work order."""
    69	
    70	    carrier: PlatformCarrier = field(default_factory=PlatformCarrier)
    71	
    72	    @property
    73	    def secrets(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    74	        """Every secret these settings hold, for redaction.
    75	
    76	        One place to ask, exactly as the configuration's own secrets have
    77	        one, so a fourth key arriving cannot fall out of the scrubbing.
    78	        """
    79	        password = self.carrier.trunk_password
    80	        return () if password is None else (password,)
    81	
    82	    @classmethod
    83	    def from_document(cls, written: Any) -> PlatformSettings:
    84	        """The platform block of a validated spec, or the empty settings.
    85	
    86	        The schema has already refused a field nobody writes, so the reads
    87	        below take what is there at face value — the same bargain the rest
    88	        of this module makes.
    89	        """
    90	        block = written or {}
    91	        carrier = block.get("carrier") or {}
    92	        return cls(
    93	            carrier=PlatformCarrier(
    94	                trunk_address=carrier.get("trunk_address"),
    95	                trunk_number=carrier.get("trunk_number"),
    96	                trunk_username=carrier.get("trunk_username"),
    97	                trunk_password=carrier.get("trunk_password"),
    98	            ),
    99	        )
   100	
   101	
   102	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   103	class ModelSelection:
   104	    """One pinned provider/model pair and its direct credential, when used."""
   105	
   106	    provider: str
   107	    model: str
   108	    key: str | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
   109	
   110	
   111	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   112	class SpeechSelection(ModelSelection):
   113	    """The TTS selection and the technical voice it owns."""
   114	
   115	    voice_id: str = ""
   116	    speed: float = 1.0
   117	
   118	
   119	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   120	class SelectedModels:
   121	    """The complete model selection from the pinned persona version."""
   122	
   123	    llm: ModelSelection
   124	    stt: ModelSelection
   125	    tts: SpeechSelection
   126	
   127	    @property
   128	    def secrets(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   129	        """Every direct provider credential carried by this work order."""
   130	        return tuple(key for key in (self.llm.key, self.stt.key, self.tts.key) if key)
   131	
   132	    @classmethod
   133	    def from_document(cls, written: Any) -> SelectedModels:
   134	        """Read the required, already validated model block."""
   135	        tts = written["tts"]
   136	        return cls(
   137	            llm=_selection(written["llm"]),
   138	            stt=_selection(written["stt"]),
   139	            tts=SpeechSelection(
   140	                provider=tts["provider"],
   141	                model=tts["model"],
   142	                key=tts.get("key"),
   143	                voice_id=tts["voice_id"],
   144	                speed=float(tts["speed"]),
   145	            ),
   146	        )
   147	
   148	
   149	def _selection(written: Any) -> ModelSelection:
   150	    return ModelSelection(
   151	        provider=written["provider"],
   152	        model=written["model"],
   153	        key=written.get("key"),
   154	    )
   155	
   156	
   157	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   158	class Limits:
   159	    """The walls around one simulation, from the spec that claimed it.
   160	
   161	    A limit tripping ends the simulation deliberately — reported as
   162	    ``limit_reached``, which is never the agent failing.
   163	    """
   164	
   165	    max_duration_seconds: int
   166	    max_turns: int
   167	
   168	
   169	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   170	class SimulationSpec:
   171	    """One claimable simulation, fully flattened — nothing left to resolve."""
   172	
   173	    simulation_id: str
   174	    """Opaque to the simulator: never parsed, never minted, never rewritten."""
   175	
   176	    modality: str
   177	    """``chat`` or ``voice``. Selects the pipeline legs, not the persona."""
   178	
   179	    scenario_instructions: str
   180	    """What the persona wants on this occasion, from the test's own content."""
   181	
   182	    limits: Limits
   183	
   184	    persona_traits: dict[str, Any]
   185	    """The persona version's complete authored human traits."""
   186	
   187	    agent_platform: str | None
   188	    """What runs the agent. Provenance only; never adapter dispatch."""
   189	
   190	    connection_type: str
   191	    """Which adapter reaches the agent. An open vocabulary, not an enum."""
   192	
   193	    access_variant: str
   194	    """Which explicit authority and config path the adapter uses."""
   195	
   196	    connection_config: dict[str, Any]
   197	    """The non-secret reach configuration; its keys belong to the plug."""
   198	
   199	    credentials: Any
   200	    """Secret material, or None. Held in memory, handed only to the plug."""
   201	
   202	    models: SelectedModels
   203	    """The only source for LLM, STT, TTS, and technical voice choices."""
   204	
   205	    mock_tools: tuple[MockTool, ...] = ()
   206	    """What egma answers for while this simulation runs, already resolved.
   207	
   208	    Empty is the ordinary case and means egma answers for nothing: every
   209	    tool the agent has runs its own implementation, untouched and
   210	    unobserved.
   211	    """
   212	
   213	    platform: PlatformSettings = field(default_factory=PlatformSettings)
   214	    """The optional SIP carrier block. It owns no model or voice choice."""
   215	
   216	    @classmethod
   217	    def from_document(cls, document: Any) -> SimulationSpec:
   218	        """Hold a claimed document to the contract, then read it.
   219	
   220	        Raises ``ContractViolation`` if the document does not speak the
   221	        contract — which is a refusal to conduct, not a simulation that
   222	        went wrong.
   223	        """
   224	        validate_spec(document)
   225	        connection = document["connection"]
   226	        limits = document["limits"]
   227	        return cls(
   228	            mock_tools=_mock_tools(document.get("mock_tools") or []),
   229	            platform=PlatformSettings.from_document(document.get("platform")),
   230	            models=SelectedModels.from_document(document["models"]),
   231	            simulation_id=document["simulation_id"],
   232	            modality=document["modality"],
   233	            scenario_instructions=document["scenario"]["instructions"],
   234	            limits=Limits(
   235	                max_duration_seconds=limits["max_duration_seconds"],
   236	                max_turns=limits["max_turns"],
   237	            ),
   238	            persona_traits=document["persona"]["traits"],
   239	            agent_platform=connection["agent_platform"],
   240	            connection_type=connection["connection_type"],
   241	            access_variant=connection["access_variant"],
   242	            connection_config=connection["config"],
   243	            credentials=connection["credentials"],
   244	        )
   245	
   246	
   247	def _mock_tools(written: list[Any]) -> tuple[MockTool, ...]:
   248	    """The resolved answers, one per tool name.
   249	
   250	    The one thing the schema cannot say is that two entries must not name
   251	    the same tool — matching is by name and nothing else, so two answers
   252	    for one name are two answers with no rule to choose between them. It
   253	    is refused rather than resolved here: taking either one silently would
   254	    make the record's answer a matter of which the control plane happened
   255	    to write first.
   256	    """
   257	    named: dict[str, MockTool] = {}
   258	    for entry in written:
   259	        tool_name = entry["tool_name"]
   260	        if tool_name in named:
   261	            raise ContractViolation(
   262	                "spec",
   263	                [
   264	                    f"/mock_tools: {tool_name!r} is answered twice, and "
   265	                    "matching is by name alone — there is no rule that would "
   266	                    "choose between them"
   267	                ],
   268	            )

   118	class OpenAICompatibleModel:
   119	    """The direct OpenAI adapter behind the model-client seam.
   120	
   121	    The pinned persona version supplies the model and the claim supplies the
   122	    current key. CI never selects this client.
   123	    """
   124	
   125	    def __init__(
   126	        self,
   127	        *,
   128	        base_url: str,
   129	        api_key: str,
   130	        model_name: str,
   131	        timeout_seconds: float = MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   132	    ) -> None:
   133	        self._base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
   134	        self._api_key = api_key
   135	        self._model_name = model_name
   136	        self._timeout = aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=timeout_seconds)
   137	        self._session: aiohttp.ClientSession | None = None
   138	
   139	    @property
   140	    def model_name(self) -> str:
   141	        return self._model_name
   142	
   143	    def _live_session(self) -> aiohttp.ClientSession:
   144	        if self._session is None:
   145	            self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession()
   146	        return self._session
   147	
   148	    def _provider_detail(self, value: object) -> str:
   149	        """A bounded provider detail with this client's credential removed.
   150	
   151	        Model failures cross Pipecat's traced service seam. Pipecat records
   152	        exception messages on its native span, before the simulation lifecycle
   153	        applies its process-wide redactor, so the client must remove the key at
   154	        the source.
   155	        """
   156	        rendered = value if isinstance(value, str) else repr(value)
   157	        return self._without_api_key(rendered)[:200]
   158	
   159	    def _without_api_key(self, text: str) -> str:
   160	        """Remove this client's bearer key from provider-authored text.
   161	
   162	        A one-character development key such as ``k`` must not rewrite every
   163	        word containing that letter. Short keys are therefore removed when
   164	        they appear as their own token, which still covers an echoed bearer,
   165	        JSON value, URL parameter, or provider sentence. Real provider keys are
   166	        long enough to replace exactly wherever they occur.
   167	        """
   168	        if not self._api_key:
   169	            return text
   170	        if len(self._api_key) >= 8:
   171	            return text.replace(self._api_key, REDACTED)
   172	        return re.sub(
   173	            rf"(?<![{_SHORT_SECRET_CHARS}]){re.escape(self._api_key)}"
   174	            rf"(?![{_SHORT_SECRET_CHARS}])",
   175	            REDACTED,
   176	            text,
   177	        )
   178	
   179	    async def reply(self, messages: list[dict[str, str]]) -> PersonaReply:
   180	        asked = {"model": self._model_name, "messages": messages}
   181	        try:
   182	            async with self._live_session().post(
   183	                f"{self._base_url}/chat/completions",
   184	                json=asked,
   185	                headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self._api_key}"},
   186	                timeout=self._timeout,
   187	            ) as response:
   188	                if response.status != 200:
   189	                    raise ModelFailure(
   190	                        f"the model answered {response.status}: "
   191	                        f"{self._provider_detail(await response.text())}"
   192	                    )
   193	                body = await response.json()
   194	        except UNREACHABLE as error:
   195	            raise ModelFailure(
   196	                f"the model was unreachable: {self._provider_detail(error)}"
   197	            ) from None
   198	
   199	        try:
   200	            content = body["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
   201	        except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError) as unexpected:
   202	            raise ModelFailure(
   203	                "the model's answer had no message content: "
   204	                f"{self._provider_detail(body)}"
   205	            ) from unexpected
   206	        if not isinstance(content, str):
   207	            raise ModelFailure(
   208	                f"the model's content was not text: {self._provider_detail(content)}"
   209	            )
   210	
   211	        content = self._without_api_key(content)
   212	        concluded = CONCLUDE_MARKER in content
   213	        text = content.replace(CONCLUDE_MARKER, "").strip()
   214	        if not text:
   215	            raise ModelFailure("the model's answer had no words to speak")

   217	
   218	    async def close(self) -> None:
   219	        if self._session is not None:
   220	            await self._session.close()
   221	            self._session = None

     6	voice, and a speech-to-text leg turning what comes back into the

     8	speaking rather than for words — the voice activity detector. It is an
     9	internal simulator choice, not authored persona data.

    12	real provider's service sits — Cartesia or OpenAI speaking, and Deepgram
    13	or OpenAI Realtime listening —

    15	The listening leg goes further and is a Pipecat STT service, the very
    16	class a real one subclasses; the speaking leg deliberately is not, and
    17	:class:`ScriptedTTS` says why.

    19	**Which pair is used comes only from the claimed models block.** The
    20	scripted pair is an explicit unit-test injection. Runtime work orders never
    21	fall back to it or combine it with one selected provider leg.

    24	little-endian mono, at whatever band the transport carries — and it is
    25	exactly invertible: each UTF-8 byte of the text becomes one fixed-length
    26	tone whose frequency names the byte. The STT reads nothing but the samples

    28	smuggling the text past it, and a recording of the exchange can be read
    29	back the same way — which is how a test tells which speaker is on which

   121	# -- The scripted codec ------------------------------------------------------
   122	
   123	
   124	@cache
   125	def _tones(sample_rate_hz: int) -> tuple[dict[int, bytes], dict[bytes, int]]:
   126	    """The tone for every byte at one band, and the way back.
   127	
   128	    A cosine rather than a sine so no tone opens on a zero sample: silence
   129	    is then exactly the samples nobody spoke into, which is what makes the
   130	    leading quiet before an answer measurable.
   131	    """
   132	    forward: dict[int, bytes] = {}
   133	    for value in range(256):
   134	        hertz = TONE_BASE_HZ + value * TONE_STEP_HZ
   135	        forward[value] = b"".join(
   136	            struct.pack(
   137	                "<h",
   138	                int(
   139	                    TONE_AMPLITUDE * math.cos(2 * math.pi * hertz * n / sample_rate_hz)
   140	                ),
   141	            )
   142	            for n in range(SAMPLES_PER_BYTE)
   143	        )
   144	    return forward, {tone: value for value, tone in forward.items()}
   145	
   146	
   147	def encode_speech(text: str, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   148	    """One utterance, spoken: PCM at the band the transport carries."""
   149	    forward, _ = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   150	    return b"".join(forward[byte] for byte in text.encode())
   151	
   152	
   153	def silence(seconds: float, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   154	    """Quiet of a given length, in the same sample format as speech."""
   155	    samples = int(round(seconds * sample_rate_hz))
   156	    return bytes(max(samples, 0) * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES)
   157	
   158	
   159	def leading_silence_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   160	    """How long nobody spoke at the start of one stretch of audio."""
   161	    quiet = 0
   162	    for offset in range(0, len(pcm) - 1, SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES):
   163	        if pcm[offset] or pcm[offset + 1]:
   164	            break
   165	        quiet += 1
   166	    return quiet / sample_rate_hz
   167	
   168	
   169	def duration_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   170	    """How long one stretch of audio lasts, from the samples themselves."""
   171	    return len(pcm) / SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES / sample_rate_hz
   172	
   173	
   174	def spoken_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   175	    """How long the speaking part of one stretch of audio lasts.
   176	
   177	    The quiet before a speaker starts is measured on its own, as
   178	    time-to-first-word, so the two measures add up to the whole rather
   179	    than counting the same silence twice.
   180	    """
   181	    return duration_seconds(pcm, sample_rate_hz) - leading_silence_seconds(
   182	        pcm, sample_rate_hz
   183	    )
   184	
   185	
   186	def peak_level(pcm: bytes) -> int:
   187	    """The loudest sample in one stretch of audio.
   188	
   189	    PCM is always little-endian and ``array`` holds samples in this
   190	    machine's byte order, so the two agree only on a little-endian
   191	    machine and a swap is what makes them agree anywhere else.
   192	    """
   193	    samples = array("h")
   194	    samples.frombytes(pcm[: len(pcm) // SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES])
   195	    if sys.byteorder != "little":
   196	        samples.byteswap()
   197	    return max((abs(sample) for sample in samples), default=0)
   198	
   199	
   200	def carries_speech(pcm: bytes) -> bool:
   201	    """Whether somebody is talking in this stretch of audio."""
   202	    return peak_level(pcm) >= SPEECH_LEVEL
   203	
   204	
   205	def decode_speech(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> str:
   206	    """What was said, read out of the samples and nothing else.
   207	
   208	    Alignment is not assumed. An utterance handed straight from the TTS
   209	    starts on a tone boundary, but the same audio inside a recording sits
   210	    after however much quiet the two speakers left between them, so the
   211	    reader slides a sample at a time until a tone lands and then runs
   212	    tone by tone until one does not.
   213	    """
   214	    _, backward = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   215	    width = SAMPLES_PER_BYTE * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   216	    said = bytearray()
   217	    offset = 0
   218	    while offset + width <= len(pcm):
   219	        value = backward.get(pcm[offset : offset + width])
   220	        if value is None:
   221	            offset += SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   222	            continue
   223	        said.append(value)
   224	        offset += width
   225	    return said.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

   231	class ScriptedTTS(FrameProcessor):
   232	    """The persona's voice, deterministically.
   233	
   234	    Holds the voice the persona was authored with the way a real service
   235	    holds a provider voice id — the exchange is what proves the leg was
   236	    assembled from this simulation's own spec.
   237	
   238	    **Why this one is not built on Pipecat's TTS service, when the
   239	    listening leg is built on Pipecat's STT service.** That base class
   240	    regroups whatever it is given back into sentences, and it does the
   241	    grouping with NLTK, whose corpus is fetched from the internet the
   242	    first time it is wanted. On a machine without that corpus the
   243	    grouping raises, the turn's audio is dropped, and the recording
   244	    quietly loses a persona turn while the transcript still shows it —
   245	    found by starving a run of the corpus and reading the channels back.
   246	    There is no way to hand that base class a different grouper.
   247	
   248	    So this leg is a plain frame processor emitting exactly the frames the
   249	    base class emits, in the same place in the chain. A real provider is
   250	    still an ordinary Pipecat TTS service dropped into that same place —
   251	    what it is not is *this* leg's base class, and CI needs no corpus and
   252	    no network to speak.

   262	        # A transcription is a text frame travelling the other way — the
   263	        # agent's words on their way to the persona, never something to
   264	        # speak. The service base class draws the same line.
   265	        if isinstance(frame, StartFrame):

   268	            frame, TranscriptionFrame | InterimTranscriptionFrame
   269	        ):
   270	            await self._speak(frame.text)

    91	class ScriptedModel:
    92	    """Deterministic persona turns derived from the scenario instructions.
    93	
    94	    Which sentence comes next is read off the messages themselves — the
    95	    count of ``assistant`` turns already spoken — so the reply is a pure
    96	    function of its input and identical across resends, restarts, and
    97	    reruns. When the script is spent, the persona says a fixed goodbye and

   106	        return "scripted"
   107	
   108	    async def reply(self, messages: list[dict[str, str]]) -> PersonaReply:
   109	        spoken = sum(1 for message in messages if message["role"] == "assistant")

   111	            return PersonaReply(text=self._script[spoken], concluded=False)

   114	    async def close(self) -> None:

   118	class OpenAICompatibleModel:
   119	    """The direct OpenAI adapter behind the model-client seam.
   120	
   121	    The pinned persona version supplies the model and the claim supplies the
   122	    current key. CI never selects this client.
   123	    """
   124	
   125	    def __init__(
   126	        self,
   127	        *,
   128	        base_url: str,
   129	        api_key: str,
   130	        model_name: str,
   131	        timeout_seconds: float = MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   132	    ) -> None:
   133	        self._base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
   134	        self._api_key = api_key
   135	        self._model_name = model_name
   136	        self._timeout = aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=timeout_seconds)
   137	        self._session: aiohttp.ClientSession | None = None
   138	
   139	    @property
   140	    def model_name(self) -> str:
   141	        return self._model_name
   142	
   143	    def _live_session(self) -> aiohttp.ClientSession:
   144	        if self._session is None:
   145	            self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession()
   146	        return self._session
   147	
   148	    def _provider_detail(self, value: object) -> str:
   149	        """A bounded provider detail with this client's credential removed.
   150	
   151	        Model failures cross Pipecat's traced service seam. Pipecat records
   152	        exception messages on its native span, before the simulation lifecycle
   153	        applies its process-wide redactor, so the client must remove the key at
   154	        the source.
   155	        """
   156	        rendered = value if isinstance(value, str) else repr(value)
   157	        return self._without_api_key(rendered)[:200]
   158	
   159	    def _without_api_key(self, text: str) -> str:
   160	        """Remove this client's bearer key from provider-authored text.
   161	
   162	        A one-character development key such as ``k`` must not rewrite every
   163	        word containing that letter. Short keys are therefore removed when
   164	        they appear as their own token, which still covers an echoed bearer,
   165	        JSON value, URL parameter, or provider sentence. Real provider keys are
   166	        long enough to replace exactly wherever they occur.
   167	        """
   168	        if not self._api_key:
   169	            return text
   170	        if len(self._api_key) >= 8:
   171	            return text.replace(self._api_key, REDACTED)
   172	        return re.sub(
   173	            rf"(?<![{_SHORT_SECRET_CHARS}]){re.escape(self._api_key)}"
   174	            rf"(?![{_SHORT_SECRET_CHARS}])",
   175	            REDACTED,
   176	            text,
   177	        )
   178	
   179	    async def reply(self, messages: list[dict[str, str]]) -> PersonaReply:
   180	        asked = {"model": self._model_name, "messages": messages}
   181	        try:
   182	            async with self._live_session().post(
   183	                f"{self._base_url}/chat/completions",
   184	                json=asked,
   185	                headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self._api_key}"},
   186	                timeout=self._timeout,
   187	            ) as response:
   188	                if response.status != 200:
   189	                    raise ModelFailure(
   190	                        f"the model answered {response.status}: "
   191	                        f"{self._provider_detail(await response.text())}"
   192	                    )
   193	                body = await response.json()
   194	        except UNREACHABLE as error:
   195	            raise ModelFailure(
   196	                f"the model was unreachable: {self._provider_detail(error)}"
   197	            ) from None
   198	
   199	        try:
   200	            content = body["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
   201	        except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError) as unexpected:
   202	            raise ModelFailure(
   203	                "the model's answer had no message content: "
   204	                f"{self._provider_detail(body)}"
   205	            ) from unexpected
   206	        if not isinstance(content, str):
   207	            raise ModelFailure(
   208	                f"the model's content was not text: {self._provider_detail(content)}"
   209	            )
   210	
   211	        content = self._without_api_key(content)
   212	        concluded = CONCLUDE_MARKER in content
   213	        text = content.replace(CONCLUDE_MARKER, "").strip()
   214	        if not text:
   215	            raise ModelFailure("the model's answer had no words to speak")

   217	
   218	    async def close(self) -> None:
   219	        if self._session is not None:
   220	            await self._session.close()
   221	            self._session = None

     6	voice, and a speech-to-text leg turning what comes back into the

     8	speaking rather than for words — the voice activity detector. It is an
     9	internal simulator choice, not authored persona data.

    11	Both legs are ordinary Pipecat frame processors, in the two places a
    12	real provider's service sits — Cartesia or OpenAI speaking, and Deepgram
    13	or OpenAI Realtime listening —

    15	The listening leg goes further and is a Pipecat STT service, the very
    16	class a real one subclasses; the speaking leg deliberately is not, and
    17	:class:`ScriptedTTS` says why.
    18	
    19	**Which pair is used comes only from the claimed models block.** The
    20	scripted pair is an explicit unit-test injection. Runtime work orders never
    21	fall back to it or combine it with one selected provider leg.

    24	little-endian mono, at whatever band the transport carries — and it is
    25	exactly invertible: each UTF-8 byte of the text becomes one fixed-length
    26	tone whose frequency names the byte. The STT reads nothing but the samples

    28	smuggling the text past it, and a recording of the exchange can be read
    29	back the same way — which is how a test tells which speaker is on which

   123	
   124	@cache
   125	def _tones(sample_rate_hz: int) -> tuple[dict[int, bytes], dict[bytes, int]]:
   126	    """The tone for every byte at one band, and the way back.
   127	
   128	    A cosine rather than a sine so no tone opens on a zero sample: silence
   129	    is then exactly the samples nobody spoke into, which is what makes the
   130	    leading quiet before an answer measurable.
   131	    """
   132	    forward: dict[int, bytes] = {}
   133	    for value in range(256):
   134	        hertz = TONE_BASE_HZ + value * TONE_STEP_HZ
   135	        forward[value] = b"".join(
   136	            struct.pack(
   137	                "<h",
   138	                int(
   139	                    TONE_AMPLITUDE * math.cos(2 * math.pi * hertz * n / sample_rate_hz)
   140	                ),
   141	            )
   142	            for n in range(SAMPLES_PER_BYTE)
   143	        )
   144	    return forward, {tone: value for value, tone in forward.items()}
   145	
   146	
   147	def encode_speech(text: str, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   148	    """One utterance, spoken: PCM at the band the transport carries."""
   149	    forward, _ = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   150	    return b"".join(forward[byte] for byte in text.encode())
   151	
   152	
   153	def silence(seconds: float, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   154	    """Quiet of a given length, in the same sample format as speech."""
   155	    samples = int(round(seconds * sample_rate_hz))
   156	    return bytes(max(samples, 0) * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES)
   157	
   158	
   159	def leading_silence_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   160	    """How long nobody spoke at the start of one stretch of audio."""
   161	    quiet = 0
   162	    for offset in range(0, len(pcm) - 1, SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES):
   163	        if pcm[offset] or pcm[offset + 1]:
   164	            break
   165	        quiet += 1
   166	    return quiet / sample_rate_hz
   167	
   168	
   169	def duration_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   170	    """How long one stretch of audio lasts, from the samples themselves."""
   171	    return len(pcm) / SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES / sample_rate_hz
   172	
   173	
   174	def spoken_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   175	    """How long the speaking part of one stretch of audio lasts.
   176	
   177	    The quiet before a speaker starts is measured on its own, as
   178	    time-to-first-word, so the two measures add up to the whole rather
   179	    than counting the same silence twice.
   180	    """
   181	    return duration_seconds(pcm, sample_rate_hz) - leading_silence_seconds(
   182	        pcm, sample_rate_hz
   183	    )
   184	
   185	
   186	def peak_level(pcm: bytes) -> int:
   187	    """The loudest sample in one stretch of audio.
   188	
   189	    PCM is always little-endian and ``array`` holds samples in this
   190	    machine's byte order, so the two agree only on a little-endian
   191	    machine and a swap is what makes them agree anywhere else.
   192	    """
   193	    samples = array("h")
   194	    samples.frombytes(pcm[: len(pcm) // SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES])
   195	    if sys.byteorder != "little":
   196	        samples.byteswap()
   197	    return max((abs(sample) for sample in samples), default=0)
   198	
   199	
   200	def carries_speech(pcm: bytes) -> bool:
   201	    """Whether somebody is talking in this stretch of audio."""
   202	    return peak_level(pcm) >= SPEECH_LEVEL
   203	
   204	
   205	def decode_speech(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> str:
   206	    """What was said, read out of the samples and nothing else.
   207	
   208	    Alignment is not assumed. An utterance handed straight from the TTS
   209	    starts on a tone boundary, but the same audio inside a recording sits
   210	    after however much quiet the two speakers left between them, so the
   211	    reader slides a sample at a time until a tone lands and then runs
   212	    tone by tone until one does not.
   213	    """
   214	    _, backward = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   215	    width = SAMPLES_PER_BYTE * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   216	    said = bytearray()
   217	    offset = 0
   218	    while offset + width <= len(pcm):
   219	        value = backward.get(pcm[offset : offset + width])
   220	        if value is None:
   221	            offset += SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   222	            continue
   223	        said.append(value)
   224	        offset += width
   225	    return said.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

   231	class ScriptedTTS(FrameProcessor):
   232	    """The persona's voice, deterministically.
   233	
   234	    Holds the voice the persona was authored with the way a real service
   235	    holds a provider voice id — the exchange is what proves the leg was
   236	    assembled from this simulation's own spec.
   237	
   238	    **Why this one is not built on Pipecat's TTS service, when the
   239	    listening leg is built on Pipecat's STT service.** That base class
   240	    regroups whatever it is given back into sentences, and it does the
   241	    grouping with NLTK, whose corpus is fetched from the internet the
   242	    first time it is wanted. On a machine without that corpus the
   243	    grouping raises, the turn's audio is dropped, and the recording
   244	    quietly loses a persona turn while the transcript still shows it —
   245	    found by starving a run of the corpus and reading the channels back.
   246	    There is no way to hand that base class a different grouper.
   247	
   248	    So this leg is a plain frame processor emitting exactly the frames the

   247	def _mock_tools(written: list[Any]) -> tuple[MockTool, ...]:
   248	    """The resolved answers, one per tool name.
   249	
   250	    The one thing the schema cannot say is that two entries must not name
   251	    the same tool — matching is by name and nothing else, so two answers
   252	    for one name are two answers with no rule to choose between them. It
   253	    is refused rather than resolved here: taking either one silently would
   254	    make the record's answer a matter of which the control plane happened
   255	    to write first.
   256	    """
   257	    named: dict[str, MockTool] = {}
   258	    for entry in written:
   259	        tool_name = entry["tool_name"]
   260	        if tool_name in named:
   261	            raise ContractViolation(
   262	                "spec",
   263	                [
   264	                    f"/mock_tools: {tool_name!r} is answered twice, and "
   265	                    "matching is by name alone — there is no rule that would "
   266	                    "choose between them"
   267	                ],
   268	            )
   269	        named[tool_name] = MockTool(
   270	            tool_name=tool_name,
   271	            answer=entry["answer"],
   272	            delay_milliseconds=entry["delay_milliseconds"],
   273	        )
   274	    return tuple(named.values())

    94	    Which sentence comes next is read off the messages themselves — the
    95	    count of ``assistant`` turns already spoken — so the reply is a pure

   148	    def _provider_detail(self, value: object) -> str:
   149	        """A bounded provider detail with this client's credential removed.
   150	
   151	        Model failures cross Pipecat's traced service seam. Pipecat records
   152	        exception messages on its native span, before the simulation lifecycle
   153	        applies its process-wide redactor, so the client must remove the key at
   154	        the source.
   155	        """

   159	    def _without_api_key(self, text: str) -> str:

   161	
   162	        A one-character development key such as ``k`` must not rewrite every
   163	        word containing that letter. Short keys are therefore removed when
   164	        they appear as their own token, which still covers an echoed bearer,
   165	        JSON value, URL parameter, or provider sentence. Real provider keys are
   166	        long enough to replace exactly wherever they occur.
   167	        """

   173	            rf"(?<![{_SHORT_SECRET_CHARS}]){re.escape(self._api_key)}"
   174	            rf"(?![{_SHORT_SECRET_CHARS}])",
   175	            REDACTED,
   176	            text,
   177	        )

   183	                f"{self._base_url}/chat/completions",

   186	                timeout=self._timeout,

   191	                        f"{self._provider_detail(await response.text())}"

   195	            raise ModelFailure(
   196	                f"the model was unreachable: {self._provider_detail(error)}"
   197	            ) from None

   199	        try:
   200	            content = body["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
   201	        except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError) as unexpected:
   202	            raise ModelFailure(
   203	                "the model's answer had no message content: "
   204	                f"{self._provider_detail(body)}"

   208	                f"the model's content was not text: {self._provider_detail(content)}"

     2	
     3	A voice simulation is a chat simulation with two more legs. The persona
     4	brain still writes the words — it never learns that they are spoken — and
     5	these are what carry them: a text-to-speech leg giving the persona a
     6	voice, and a speech-to-text leg turning what comes back into the
     7	transcript's ``agent`` turns. A third leg listens for *whether* anybody is
     8	speaking rather than for words — the voice activity detector. It is an
     9	internal simulator choice, not authored persona data.
    10	
    11	Both legs are ordinary Pipecat frame processors, in the two places a
    12	real provider's service sits — Cartesia or OpenAI speaking, and Deepgram
    13	or OpenAI Realtime listening —
    14	so the pipeline assembled around them is the same pipeline either way.
    15	The listening leg goes further and is a Pipecat STT service, the very
    16	class a real one subclasses; the speaking leg deliberately is not, and
    17	:class:`ScriptedTTS` says why.
    18	
    19	**Which pair is used comes only from the claimed models block.** The
    20	scripted pair is an explicit unit-test injection. Runtime work orders never
    21	fall back to it or combine it with one selected provider leg.
    22

    24	little-endian mono, at whatever band the transport carries — and it is
    25	exactly invertible: each UTF-8 byte of the text becomes one fixed-length
    26	tone whose frequency names the byte. The STT reads nothing but the samples
    27	handed to it, so the loopback proves the whole audio path rather than
    28	smuggling the text past it, and a recording of the exchange can be read
    29	back the same way — which is how a test tells which speaker is on which
    30	channel.

    32	The tones stay under 3 kHz so that the narrowest band a connection can
    33	carry, 8 kHz telephony, still holds them.

   121	# -- The scripted codec ------------------------------------------------------
   122	
   123	
   124	@cache
   125	def _tones(sample_rate_hz: int) -> tuple[dict[int, bytes], dict[bytes, int]]:
   126	    """The tone for every byte at one band, and the way back.
   127	
   128	    A cosine rather than a sine so no tone opens on a zero sample: silence
   129	    is then exactly the samples nobody spoke into, which is what makes the
   130	    leading quiet before an answer measurable.
   131	    """
   132	    forward: dict[int, bytes] = {}
   133	    for value in range(256):
   134	        hertz = TONE_BASE_HZ + value * TONE_STEP_HZ
   135	        forward[value] = b"".join(
   136	            struct.pack(
   137	                "<h",
   138	                int(
   139	                    TONE_AMPLITUDE * math.cos(2 * math.pi * hertz * n / sample_rate_hz)
   140	                ),
   141	            )
   142	            for n in range(SAMPLES_PER_BYTE)
   143	        )
   144	    return forward, {tone: value for value, tone in forward.items()}
   145	
   146	
   147	def encode_speech(text: str, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   148	    """One utterance, spoken: PCM at the band the transport carries."""
   149	    forward, _ = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   150	    return b"".join(forward[byte] for byte in text.encode())
   151	
   152	
   153	def silence(seconds: float, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   154	    """Quiet of a given length, in the same sample format as speech."""
   155	    samples = int(round(seconds * sample_rate_hz))
   156	    return bytes(max(samples, 0) * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES)
   157	
   158	
   159	def leading_silence_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   160	    """How long nobody spoke at the start of one stretch of audio."""
   161	    quiet = 0
   162	    for offset in range(0, len(pcm) - 1, SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES):
   163	        if pcm[offset] or pcm[offset + 1]:
   164	            break
   165	        quiet += 1
   166	    return quiet / sample_rate_hz
   167	
   168	
   169	def duration_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   170	    """How long one stretch of audio lasts, from the samples themselves."""
   171	    return len(pcm) / SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES / sample_rate_hz
   172	
   173	
   174	def spoken_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   175	    """How long the speaking part of one stretch of audio lasts.
   176	
   177	    The quiet before a speaker starts is measured on its own, as
   178	    time-to-first-word, so the two measures add up to the whole rather
   179	    than counting the same silence twice.
   180	    """
   181	    return duration_seconds(pcm, sample_rate_hz) - leading_silence_seconds(
   182	        pcm, sample_rate_hz
   183	    )
   184	
   185	
   186	def peak_level(pcm: bytes) -> int:
   187	    """The loudest sample in one stretch of audio.
   188	
   189	    PCM is always little-endian and ``array`` holds samples in this
   190	    machine's byte order, so the two agree only on a little-endian
   191	    machine and a swap is what makes them agree anywhere else.
   192	    """
   193	    samples = array("h")
   194	    samples.frombytes(pcm[: len(pcm) // SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES])
   195	    if sys.byteorder != "little":
   196	        samples.byteswap()
   197	    return max((abs(sample) for sample in samples), default=0)
   198	
   199	
   200	def carries_speech(pcm: bytes) -> bool:
   201	    """Whether somebody is talking in this stretch of audio."""
   202	    return peak_level(pcm) >= SPEECH_LEVEL
   203	
   204	
   205	def decode_speech(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> str:
   206	    """What was said, read out of the samples and nothing else.
   207	
   208	    Alignment is not assumed. An utterance handed straight from the TTS
   209	    starts on a tone boundary, but the same audio inside a recording sits
   210	    after however much quiet the two speakers left between them, so the
   211	    reader slides a sample at a time until a tone lands and then runs
   212	    tone by tone until one does not.
   213	    """
   214	    _, backward = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   215	    width = SAMPLES_PER_BYTE * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   216	    said = bytearray()
   217	    offset = 0
   218	    while offset + width <= len(pcm):
   219	        value = backward.get(pcm[offset : offset + width])
   220	        if value is None:
   221	            offset += SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   222	            continue
   223	        said.append(value)
   224	        offset += width
   225	    return said.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

   231	class ScriptedTTS(FrameProcessor):
   232	    """The persona's voice, deterministically.
   233	
   234	    Holds the voice the persona was authored with the way a real service
   235	    holds a provider voice id — the exchange is what proves the leg was
   236	    assembled from this simulation's own spec.
   237	
   238	    **Why this one is not built on Pipecat's TTS service, when the
   239	    listening leg is built on Pipecat's STT service.** That base class
   240	    regroups whatever it is given back into sentences, and it does the
   241	    grouping with NLTK, whose corpus is fetched from the internet the
   242	    first time it is wanted. On a machine without that corpus the
   243	    grouping raises, the turn's audio is dropped, and the recording
   244	    quietly loses a persona turn while the transcript still shows it —
   245	    found by starving a run of the corpus and reading the channels back.
   246	    There is no way to hand that base class a different grouper.
   247	
   248	    So this leg is a plain frame processor emitting exactly the frames the
   249	    base class emits, in the same place in the chain. A real provider is
   250	    still an ordinary Pipecat TTS service dropped into that same place —
   251	    what it is not is *this* leg's base class, and CI needs no corpus and
   252	    no network to speak.
   253	    """
   254	
   255	    def __init__(self, *, voice: PersonaVoice) -> None:
   256	        super().__init__()
   257	        self.voice = voice
   258	        self.sample_rate_hz = 0
   259	
   260	    async def process_frame(self, frame: Frame, direction: FrameDirection) -> None:
   261	        await super().process_frame(frame, direction)
   262	        # A transcription is a text frame travelling the other way — the
   263	        # agent's words on their way to the persona, never something to
   264	        # speak. The service base class draws the same line.
   265	        if isinstance(frame, StartFrame):
   266	            self.sample_rate_hz = frame.audio_out_sample_rate
   267	        if isinstance(frame, TextFrame) and not isinstance(
   268	            frame, TranscriptionFrame | InterimTranscriptionFrame
   269	        ):
   270	            await self._speak(frame.text)
   271	        await self.push_frame(frame, direction)
   272	
   273	    async def _speak(self, text: str) -> None:
   274	        if not text:
   275	            return
   276	        await self.push_frame(TTSStartedFrame())
   277	        await self.push_frame(
   278	            TTSAudioRawFrame(
   279	                audio=encode_speech(text, self.sample_rate_hz),
   280	                sample_rate=self.sample_rate_hz,
   281	                num_channels=1,
   282	            )
   283	        )
   284	        await self.push_frame(TTSStoppedFrame())

   144	        if self._session is None:

   148	    def _provider_detail(self, value: object) -> str:
   149	        """A bounded provider detail with this client's credential removed.
   150	
   151	        Model failures cross Pipecat's traced service seam. Pipecat records
   152	        exception messages on its native span, before the simulation lifecycle
   153	        applies its process-wide redactor, so the client must remove the key at
   154	        the source.

   159	    def _without_api_key(self, text: str) -> str:
   160	        """Remove this client's bearer key from provider-authored text.
   161	
   162	        A one-character development key such as ``k`` must not rewrite every
   163	        word containing that letter. Short keys are therefore removed when
   164	        they appear as their own token, which still covers an echoed bearer,
   165	        JSON value, URL parameter, or provider sentence. Real provider keys are
   166	        long enough to replace exactly wherever they occur.

   170	        if len(self._api_key) >= 8:

   173	            rf"(?<![{_SHORT_SECRET_CHARS}]){re.escape(self._api_key)}"
   174	            rf"(?![{_SHORT_SECRET_CHARS}])",
   175	            REDACTED,
   176	            text,
   177	        )

   130	    leading quiet before an answer measurable.

   136	            struct.pack(
   137	                "<h",
   138	                int(
   139	                    TONE_AMPLITUDE * math.cos(2 * math.pi * hertz * n / sample_rate_hz)
   140	                ),
   141	            )
   142	            for n in range(SAMPLES_PER_BYTE)
   143	        )
   144	    return forward, {tone: value for value, tone in forward.items()}

   153	def silence(seconds: float, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   154	    """Quiet of a given length, in the same sample format as speech."""
   155	    samples = int(round(seconds * sample_rate_hz))
   156	    return bytes(max(samples, 0) * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES)

   160	    """How long nobody spoke at the start of one stretch of audio."""
   161	    quiet = 0
   162	    for offset in range(0, len(pcm) - 1, SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES):
   163	        if pcm[offset] or pcm[offset + 1]:
   164	            break
   165	        quiet += 1
   166	    return quiet / sample_rate_hz

   170	    """How long one stretch of audio lasts, from the samples themselves."""
   171	    return len(pcm) / SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES / sample_rate_hz

   175	    """How long the speaking part of one stretch of audio lasts.
   176	
   177	    The quiet before a speaker starts is measured on its own, as
   178	    time-to-first-word, so the two measures add up to the whole rather
   179	    than counting the same silence twice.

   186	def peak_level(pcm: bytes) -> int:
   187	    """The loudest sample in one stretch of audio.
   188	
   189	    PCM is always little-endian and ``array`` holds samples in this
   190	    machine's byte order, so the two agree only on a little-endian
   191	    machine and a swap is what makes them agree anywhere else.
   192	    """
   193	    samples = array("h")
   194	    samples.frombytes(pcm[: len(pcm) // SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES])
   195	    if sys.byteorder != "little":
   196	        samples.byteswap()
   197	    return max((abs(sample) for sample in samples), default=0)

   201	    """Whether somebody is talking in this stretch of audio."""
   202	    return peak_level(pcm) >= SPEECH_LEVEL

   205	def decode_speech(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> str:
   206	    """What was said, read out of the samples and nothing else.
   207	
   208	    Alignment is not assumed. An utterance handed straight from the TTS
   209	    starts on a tone boundary, but the same audio inside a recording sits
   210	    after however much quiet the two speakers left between them, so the
   211	    reader slides a sample at a time until a tone lands and then runs
   212	    tone by tone until one does not.
   213	    """
   214	    _, backward = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   215	    width = SAMPLES_PER_BYTE * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   216	    said = bytearray()
   217	    offset = 0
   218	    while offset + width <= len(pcm):
   219	        value = backward.get(pcm[offset : offset + width])
   220	        if value is None:
   221	            offset += SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   222	            continue
   223	        said.append(value)
   224	        offset += width
   225	    return said.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

   231	class ScriptedTTS(FrameProcessor):
   232	    """The persona's voice, deterministically.
   233	
   234	    Holds the voice the persona was authored with the way a real service
   235	    holds a provider voice id — the exchange is what proves the leg was
   236	    assembled from this simulation's own spec.
   237	
   238	    **Why this one is not built on Pipecat's TTS service, when the
   239	    listening leg is built on Pipecat's STT service.** That base class
   240	    regroups whatever it is given back into sentences, and it does the
   241	    grouping with NLTK, whose corpus is fetched from the internet the
   242	    first time it is wanted. On a machine without that corpus the
   243	    grouping raises, the turn's audio is dropped, and the recording
   244	    quietly loses a persona turn while the transcript still shows it —
   245	    found by starving a run of the corpus and reading the channels back.
   246	    There is no way to hand that base class a different grouper.
   247	
   248	    So this leg is a plain frame processor emitting exactly the frames the
   249	    base class emits, in the same place in the chain. A real provider is
   250	    still an ordinary Pipecat TTS service dropped into that same place —
   251	    what it is not is *this* leg's base class, and CI needs no corpus and
   252	    no network to speak.
   253	    """
   254	
   255	    def __init__(self, *, voice: PersonaVoice) -> None:
   256	        super().__init__()
   257	        self.voice = voice
   258	        self.sample_rate_hz = 0
   259	
   260	    async def process_frame(self, frame: Frame, direction: FrameDirection) -> None:
   261	        await super().process_frame(frame, direction)
   262	        # A transcription is a text frame travelling the other way — the
   263	        # agent's words on their way to the persona, never something to
   264	        # speak. The service base class draws the same line.
   265	        if isinstance(frame, StartFrame):
   266	            self.sample_rate_hz = frame.audio_out_sample_rate
   267	        if isinstance(frame, TextFrame) and not isinstance(
   268	            frame, TranscriptionFrame | InterimTranscriptionFrame
   269	        ):
   270	            await self._speak(frame.text)
   271	        await self.push_frame(frame, direction)
   272	
   273	    async def _speak(self, text: str) -> None:
   274	        if not text:
   275	            return
   276	        await self.push_frame(TTSStartedFrame())
   277	        await self.push_frame(
   278	            TTSAudioRawFrame(
   279	                audio=encode_speech(text, self.sample_rate_hz),
   280	                sample_rate=self.sample_rate_hz,
   281	                num_channels=1,
   282	            )
   283	        )

   387	    is reported failed, and the reason on the record is what tells a

   435	        builder below accepts the scripted leg only for direct unit tests.

   546	def build_vad(providers: SpeechProviders) -> VADAnalyzer:
   547	    """The leg this simulation hears speech *starting and stopping* with.
   548	
   549	    Chosen at assembly and nowhere else, exactly like the mouth and the
   550	    ears: the scripted detector reads the test codec's samples, so CI's
   551	    every speech boundary is a sample position and the same one every
   552	    run; Silero is what a live simulation listens with, and it is asked
   553	    for by name because loading a model is a cost only a deployment that
   554	    wants it should pay.
   555	    """
   556	    providers = providers.checked()
   557	    if providers.vad != "silero":
   558	        return ScriptedVAD()
   559	
   560	    # Imported here and not at the top of the file, for the reason every
   561	    # provider in this module is: an unconfigured simulator must not load
   562	    # a model it will never run. The quarantine suite holds this.
   563	    from pipecat.audio.vad.silero import SileroVADAnalyzer
   564	
   565	    detector = SileroVADAnalyzer(params=CONVERSATION_VAD)
   566	    if getattr(detector, "_last_reset_time", None) != 0:
   567	        raise SpeechFault(
   568	            "the pinned pipecat release changed the silero state-reset seam"

   571	    # seconds. On telephone line noise that can create speech which is not
   572	    # there. A fresh detector is built for every simulation, so its model is
   573	    # already clean at the stream boundary and must keep that state until the
   574	    # simulation ends.
   575	    detector._last_reset_time = math.inf

   161	
   162	        A one-character development key such as ``k`` must not rewrite every
   163	        word containing that letter. Short keys are therefore removed when
   164	        they appear as their own token, which still covers an echoed bearer,
   165	        JSON value, URL parameter, or provider sentence. Real provider keys are
   166	        long enough to replace exactly wherever they occur.

   176	            text,
   177	        )

     2	
     3	A voice simulation is a chat simulation with two more legs. The persona
     4	brain still writes the words — it never learns that they are spoken — and
     5	these are what carry them: a text-to-speech leg giving the persona a
     6	voice, and a speech-to-text leg turning what comes back into the
     7	transcript's ``agent`` turns. A third leg listens for *whether* anybody is
     8	speaking rather than for words — the voice activity detector. It is an
     9	internal simulator choice, not authored persona data.
    10	
    11	Both legs are ordinary Pipecat frame processors, in the two places a
    12	real provider's service sits — Cartesia or OpenAI speaking, and Deepgram
    13	or OpenAI Realtime listening —
    14	so the pipeline assembled around them is the same pipeline either way.
    15	The listening leg goes further and is a Pipecat STT service, the very
    16	class a real one subclasses; the speaking leg deliberately is not, and
    17	:class:`ScriptedTTS` says why.
    18	
    19	**Which pair is used comes only from the claimed models block.** The
    20	scripted pair is an explicit unit-test injection. Runtime work orders never
    21	fall back to it or combine it with one selected provider leg.
    22	
    23	**The scripted codec.** Scripted speech is real PCM — 16-bit signed
    24	little-endian mono, at whatever band the transport carries — and it is
    25	exactly invertible: each UTF-8 byte of the text becomes one fixed-length
    26	tone whose frequency names the byte. The STT reads nothing but the samples
    27	handed to it, so the loopback proves the whole audio path rather than
    28	smuggling the text past it, and a recording of the exchange can be read
    29	back the same way — which is how a test tells which speaker is on which
    30	channel.
    31	
    32	The tones stay under 3 kHz so that the narrowest band a connection can
    33	carry, 8 kHz telephony, still holds them.

   121	# -- The scripted codec ------------------------------------------------------
   122	
   123	
   124	@cache
   125	def _tones(sample_rate_hz: int) -> tuple[dict[int, bytes], dict[bytes, int]]:
   126	    """The tone for every byte at one band, and the way back.
   127	
   128	    A cosine rather than a sine so no tone opens on a zero sample: silence
   129	    is then exactly the samples nobody spoke into, which is what makes the
   130	    leading quiet before an answer measurable.
   131	    """
   132	    forward: dict[int, bytes] = {}
   133	    for value in range(256):
   134	        hertz = TONE_BASE_HZ + value * TONE_STEP_HZ
   135	        forward[value] = b"".join(
   136	            struct.pack(
   137	                "<h",
   138	                int(
   139	                    TONE_AMPLITUDE * math.cos(2 * math.pi * hertz * n / sample_rate_hz)
   140	                ),
   141	            )
   142	            for n in range(SAMPLES_PER_BYTE)
   143	        )
   144	    return forward, {tone: value for value, tone in forward.items()}
   145	
   146	
   147	def encode_speech(text: str, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   148	    """One utterance, spoken: PCM at the band the transport carries."""
   149	    forward, _ = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   150	    return b"".join(forward[byte] for byte in text.encode())
   151	
   152	
   153	def silence(seconds: float, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   154	    """Quiet of a given length, in the same sample format as speech."""
   155	    samples = int(round(seconds * sample_rate_hz))
   156	    return bytes(max(samples, 0) * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES)
   157	
   158	
   159	def leading_silence_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   160	    """How long nobody spoke at the start of one stretch of audio."""
   161	    quiet = 0
   162	    for offset in range(0, len(pcm) - 1, SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES):
   163	        if pcm[offset] or pcm[offset + 1]:
   164	            break
   165	        quiet += 1
   166	    return quiet / sample_rate_hz
   167	
   168	
   169	def duration_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   170	    """How long one stretch of audio lasts, from the samples themselves."""
   171	    return len(pcm) / SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES / sample_rate_hz
   172	
   173	
   174	def spoken_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   175	    """How long the speaking part of one stretch of audio lasts.
   176	
   177	    The quiet before a speaker starts is measured on its own, as
   178	    time-to-first-word, so the two measures add up to the whole rather
   179	    than counting the same silence twice.
   180	    """
   181	    return duration_seconds(pcm, sample_rate_hz) - leading_silence_seconds(
   182	        pcm, sample_rate_hz
   183	    )
   184	
   185	
   186	def peak_level(pcm: bytes) -> int:
   187	    """The loudest sample in one stretch of audio.
   188	
   189	    PCM is always little-endian and ``array`` holds samples in this
   190	    machine's byte order, so the two agree only on a little-endian
   191	    machine and a swap is what makes them agree anywhere else.
   192	    """
   193	    samples = array("h")
   194	    samples.frombytes(pcm[: len(pcm) // SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES])
   195	    if sys.byteorder != "little":
   196	        samples.byteswap()
   197	    return max((abs(sample) for sample in samples), default=0)
   198	
   199	
   200	def carries_speech(pcm: bytes) -> bool:
   201	    """Whether somebody is talking in this stretch of audio."""
   202	    return peak_level(pcm) >= SPEECH_LEVEL
   203	
   204	
   205	def decode_speech(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> str:
   206	    """What was said, read out of the samples and nothing else.
   207	
   208	    Alignment is not assumed. An utterance handed straight from the TTS
   209	    starts on a tone boundary, but the same audio inside a recording sits
   210	    after however much quiet the two speakers left between them, so the
   211	    reader slides a sample at a time until a tone lands and then runs
   212	    tone by tone until one does not.
   213	    """
   214	    _, backward = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   215	    width = SAMPLES_PER_BYTE * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   216	    said = bytearray()
   217	    offset = 0
   218	    while offset + width <= len(pcm):
   219	        value = backward.get(pcm[offset : offset + width])
   220	        if value is None:
   221	            offset += SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   222	            continue
   223	        said.append(value)
   224	        offset += width
   225	    return said.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

   231	class ScriptedTTS(FrameProcessor):
   232	    """The persona's voice, deterministically.
   233	
   234	    Holds the voice the persona was authored with the way a real service
   235	    holds a provider voice id — the exchange is what proves the leg was
   236	    assembled from this simulation's own spec.
   237	
   238	    **Why this one is not built on Pipecat's TTS service, when the
   239	    listening leg is built on Pipecat's STT service.** That base class
   240	    regroups whatever it is given back into sentences, and it does the
   241	    grouping with NLTK, whose corpus is fetched from the internet the
   242	    first time it is wanted. On a machine without that corpus the
   243	    grouping raises, the turn's audio is dropped, and the recording
   244	    quietly loses a persona turn while the transcript still shows it —
   245	    found by starving a run of the corpus and reading the channels back.
   246	    There is no way to hand that base class a different grouper.
   247	
   248	    So this leg is a plain frame processor emitting exactly the frames the
   249	    base class emits, in the same place in the chain. A real provider is
   250	    still an ordinary Pipecat TTS service dropped into that same place —
   251	    what it is not is *this* leg's base class, and CI needs no corpus and
   252	    no network to speak.
   253	    """
   254	
   255	    def __init__(self, *, voice: PersonaVoice) -> None:
   256	        super().__init__()
   257	        self.voice = voice
   258	        self.sample_rate_hz = 0
   259	
   260	    async def process_frame(self, frame: Frame, direction: FrameDirection) -> None:
   261	        await super().process_frame(frame, direction)
   262	        # A transcription is a text frame travelling the other way — the
   263	        # agent's words on their way to the persona, never something to
   264	        # speak. The service base class draws the same line.
   265	        if isinstance(frame, StartFrame):
   266	            self.sample_rate_hz = frame.audio_out_sample_rate
   267	        if isinstance(frame, TextFrame) and not isinstance(
   268	            frame, TranscriptionFrame | InterimTranscriptionFrame
   269	        ):
   270	            await self._speak(frame.text)
   271	        await self.push_frame(frame, direction)

   273	    async def _speak(self, text: str) -> None:
   274	        if not text:
   275	            return
   276	        await self.push_frame(TTSStartedFrame())

   278	            TTSAudioRawFrame(
   279	                audio=encode_speech(text, self.sample_rate_hz),
   280	                sample_rate=self.sample_rate_hz,
   281	                num_channels=1,
   282	            )
   283	        )
   284	        await self.push_frame(TTSStoppedFrame())

     2	
     3	A voice simulation is a chat simulation with two more legs. The persona
     4	brain still writes the words — it never learns that they are spoken — and
     5	these are what carry them: a text-to-speech leg giving the persona a
     6	voice, and a speech-to-text leg turning what comes back into the
     7	transcript's ``agent`` turns. A third leg listens for *whether* anybody is
     8	speaking rather than for words — the voice activity detector. It is an
     9	internal simulator choice, not authored persona data.
    10	
    11	Both legs are ordinary Pipecat frame processors, in the two places a
    12	real provider's service sits — Cartesia or OpenAI speaking, and Deepgram
    13	or OpenAI Realtime listening —
    14	so the pipeline assembled around them is the same pipeline either way.
    15	The listening leg goes further and is a Pipecat STT service, the very
    16	class a real one subclasses; the speaking leg deliberately is not, and
    17	:class:`ScriptedTTS` says why.
    18	
    19	**Which pair is used comes only from the claimed models block.** The
    20	scripted pair is an explicit unit-test injection. Runtime work orders never
    21	fall back to it or combine it with one selected provider leg.
    22	
    23	**The scripted codec.** Scripted speech is real PCM — 16-bit signed
    24	little-endian mono, at whatever band the transport carries — and it is
    25	exactly invertible: each UTF-8 byte of the text becomes one fixed-length
    26	tone whose frequency names the byte. The STT reads nothing but the samples
    27	handed to it, so the loopback proves the whole audio path rather than
    28	smuggling the text past it, and a recording of the exchange can be read
    29	back the same way — which is how a test tells which speaker is on which

    70	SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES = 2
    71	"""16-bit signed little-endian, the one sample format the simulator carries."""

    73	SAMPLES_PER_BYTE = 240
    74	"""How many samples one encoded byte occupies — 30 ms at 8 kHz, 5 ms at 48 kHz."""

    76	SPEECH_LEVEL = 500
    77	"""The sample level, out of 32767, above which audio is somebody talking.
    78	
    79	A line is never digitally silent — it carries comfort noise, and a
    80	threshold is what tells that apart from speech. Set low enough to hear a
    81	quiet talker and high enough to ignore a line's own hiss.
    82	"""

    84	TONE_BASE_HZ = 200
    85	TONE_STEP_HZ = 10
    86	TONE_AMPLITUDE = 8000
    87	
    88	CARTESIA_SPEED_RANGE = (0.6, 1.5)
    89	"""What the cartesia mouth accepts as a speed multiplier, its own numbers.
    90

    95	"""How long a listening leg may take to become able to hear.
    96

    98	*silently drops* audio handed to it before that connection is up. The
    99	first thing a voice exchange does is hand it the agent's greeting, so

   121	# -- The scripted codec ------------------------------------------------------
   122	
   123	
   124	@cache
   125	def _tones(sample_rate_hz: int) -> tuple[dict[int, bytes], dict[bytes, int]]:
   126	    """The tone for every byte at one band, and the way back.
   127	
   128	    A cosine rather than a sine so no tone opens on a zero sample: silence
   129	    is then exactly the samples nobody spoke into, which is what makes the
   130	    leading quiet before an answer measurable.
   131	    """
   132	    forward: dict[int, bytes] = {}
   133	    for value in range(256):
   134	        hertz = TONE_BASE_HZ + value * TONE_STEP_HZ
   135	        forward[value] = b"".join(
   136	            struct.pack(
   137	                "<h",
   138	                int(
   139	                    TONE_AMPLITUDE * math.cos(2 * math.pi * hertz * n / sample_rate_hz)
   140	                ),
   141	            )
   142	            for n in range(SAMPLES_PER_BYTE)
   143	        )
   144	    return forward, {tone: value for value, tone in forward.items()}
   145	
   146	
   147	def encode_speech(text: str, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   148	    """One utterance, spoken: PCM at the band the transport carries."""
   149	    forward, _ = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   150	    return b"".join(forward[byte] for byte in text.encode())
   151	
   152	
   153	def silence(seconds: float, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   154	    """Quiet of a given length, in the same sample format as speech."""
   155	    samples = int(round(seconds * sample_rate_hz))
   156	    return bytes(max(samples, 0) * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES)
   157	
   158	
   159	def leading_silence_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   160	    """How long nobody spoke at the start of one stretch of audio."""
   161	    quiet = 0
   162	    for offset in range(0, len(pcm) - 1, SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES):
   163	        if pcm[offset] or pcm[offset + 1]:
   164	            break
   165	        quiet += 1
   166	    return quiet / sample_rate_hz
   167	
   168	
   169	def duration_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   170	    """How long one stretch of audio lasts, from the samples themselves."""
   171	    return len(pcm) / SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES / sample_rate_hz
   172	
   173	
   174	def spoken_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   175	    """How long the speaking part of one stretch of audio lasts.
   176	
   177	    The quiet before a speaker starts is measured on its own, as
   178	    time-to-first-word, so the two measures add up to the whole rather
   179	    than counting the same silence twice.
   180	    """
   181	    return duration_seconds(pcm, sample_rate_hz) - leading_silence_seconds(
   182	        pcm, sample_rate_hz
   183	    )
   184	
   185	
   186	def peak_level(pcm: bytes) -> int:
   187	    """The loudest sample in one stretch of audio.
   188	
   189	    PCM is always little-endian and ``array`` holds samples in this
   190	    machine's byte order, so the two agree only on a little-endian
   191	    machine and a swap is what makes them agree anywhere else.
   192	    """
   193	    samples = array("h")
   194	    samples.frombytes(pcm[: len(pcm) // SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES])
   195	    if sys.byteorder != "little":
   196	        samples.byteswap()
   197	    return max((abs(sample) for sample in samples), default=0)
   198	
   199	
   200	def carries_speech(pcm: bytes) -> bool:
   201	    """Whether somebody is talking in this stretch of audio."""
   202	    return peak_level(pcm) >= SPEECH_LEVEL
   203	
   204	
   205	def decode_speech(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> str:
   206	    """What was said, read out of the samples and nothing else.
   207	
   208	    Alignment is not assumed. An utterance handed straight from the TTS
   209	    starts on a tone boundary, but the same audio inside a recording sits
   210	    after however much quiet the two speakers left between them, so the
   211	    reader slides a sample at a time until a tone lands and then runs
   212	    tone by tone until one does not.
   213	    """
   214	    _, backward = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   215	    width = SAMPLES_PER_BYTE * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   216	    said = bytearray()
   217	    offset = 0
   218	    while offset + width <= len(pcm):
   219	        value = backward.get(pcm[offset : offset + width])
   220	        if value is None:
   221	            offset += SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   222	            continue
   223	        said.append(value)
   224	        offset += width
   225	    return said.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

   231	class ScriptedTTS(FrameProcessor):
   232	    """The persona's voice, deterministically.
   233	
   234	    Holds the voice the persona was authored with the way a real service
   235	    holds a provider voice id — the exchange is what proves the leg was
   236	    assembled from this simulation's own spec.
   237	
   238	    **Why this one is not built on Pipecat's TTS service, when the
   239	    listening leg is built on Pipecat's STT service.** That base class
   240	    regroups whatever it is given back into sentences, and it does the
   241	    grouping with NLTK, whose corpus is fetched from the internet the
   242	    first time it is wanted. On a machine without that corpus the
   243	    grouping raises, the turn's audio is dropped, and the recording
   244	    quietly loses a persona turn while the transcript still shows it —
   245	    found by starving a run of the corpus and reading the channels back.
   246	    There is no way to hand that base class a different grouper.
   247	
   248	    So this leg is a plain frame processor emitting exactly the frames the
   249	    base class emits, in the same place in the chain. A real provider is
   250	    still an ordinary Pipecat TTS service dropped into that same place —
   251	    what it is not is *this* leg's base class, and CI needs no corpus and
   252	    no network to speak.
   253	    """
   254	
   255	    def __init__(self, *, voice: PersonaVoice) -> None:
   256	        super().__init__()
   257	        self.voice = voice
   258	        self.sample_rate_hz = 0
   259	
   260	    async def process_frame(self, frame: Frame, direction: FrameDirection) -> None:
   261	        await super().process_frame(frame, direction)
   262	        # A transcription is a text frame travelling the other way — the
   263	        # agent's words on their way to the persona, never something to
   264	        # speak. The service base class draws the same line.
   265	        if isinstance(frame, StartFrame):
   266	            self.sample_rate_hz = frame.audio_out_sample_rate
   267	        if isinstance(frame, TextFrame) and not isinstance(
   268	            frame, TranscriptionFrame | InterimTranscriptionFrame
   269	        ):
   270	            await self._speak(frame.text)
   271	        await self.push_frame(frame, direction)
   272	
   273	    async def _speak(self, text: str) -> None:
   274	        if not text:
   275	            return
   276	        await self.push_frame(TTSStartedFrame())
   277	        await self.push_frame(
   278	            TTSAudioRawFrame(
   279	                audio=encode_speech(text, self.sample_rate_hz),
   280	                sample_rate=self.sample_rate_hz,
   281	                num_channels=1,
   282	            )
   283	        )
   284	        await self.push_frame(TTSStoppedFrame())

   382	class SpeechFault(RuntimeError):
   383	    """A speech leg could not be built, or could not be made able to hear.
   384	
   385	    Deliberately not a ``PlugError``: that word names a platform refusing,
   386	    and this is the persona's own mouth or ears. Either way the simulation
   387	    is reported failed, and the reason on the record is what tells a
   388	    reader which of the two happened. Voice only, and raised out of the
   389	    voice conductor: the walk has no speech legs to hear one from.
   390	    """

   393	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   394	class SpeechProviders:
   395	    """The speech adapters resolved from one pinned persona version."""

   397	    stt: str = "scripted"

   401	    reads the test codec exactly and needs no model; ``silero`` is the
   402	    production detector, and it ships inside the pinned pipecat wheel, so
   403	    choosing it downloads nothing."""

   405	    stt_key: str | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
   406	    tts_key: str | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
   407	    """The direct credential for each selected leg."""
   408	
   409	    stt_model: str | None = None

   411	    """The exact pinned models. Runtime code supplies no default."""

   413	    @classmethod
